data.title: JPMorgan Says Vendor Cyberattack May Have Exposed Customer Information
data.description: According to Jin10, JPMorgan said some of its vendors were hit by a cyberattack and attackers may have accessed some customer information. Based on its investigation so far, the bank believes the attackers accessed marketing data held by the vendors, which may include customer names and email addresses. JPMorgan did not name the affected vendors or disclose how many customers may have been affected. The bank said the incident did not disrupt its services and that it would contact affected customers and offer support, including credit monitoring. Earlier this week, JPMorgan had a service outage that affected customers; the bank said it was unrelated to cybersecurity and to the vendor attack. The report described the earlier outage as one of a recent series of digital-system problems that have raised concerns about the security of technology systems supporting large U.S. companies.

data.title: AI TRENDS | WalletConnect Launches AI Agent Service for Onchain Actions Through Claude and Other Clients
data.description:
WalletConnect announced WalletConnect for Agents, a service that connects AI clients to users’ existing wallets through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). According to Foresight News, clients including Claude, Claude Code, and Cursor can check balances and prepare transfers and token swaps, but users must approve and sign each transaction in their wallet app.

WalletConnect said the service does not hold users’ signing keys and includes per-transaction limits, a supported-token list, and a five-minute validity period for transaction plans. Token approvals are limited to the amount required for each transaction, with no unlimited approvals. Developers can also connect the features to agent workflows through an HTTP API. Access is being rolled out gradually through a waitlist.

data.title: Ledger CTO Charles Guillemet to Leave at End of 2026 After Nine Years, Build Security Project
data.description:
Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet said he will leave the crypto hardware wallet maker at the end of 2026, concluding nine years at the company. According to Foresight News, Ledger has been preparing for the transition for several months, while Guillemet is developing a new project focused on security and plans to share more details soon.

Guillemet joined Ledger in December 2017 as chief security officer, founded its security research laboratory Donjon, and later became CTO. Donjon has researched smartphone secure boot mechanisms, disclosed hardware, software, and infrastructure vulnerabilities, and conducted research on post-quantum cryptography and AI security.

Guillemet said Ledger has sold more than 8 million signing devices across 180 countries, protecting about 20% of global crypto assets. Ledger Enterprise serves more than 100 financial institutions and brands. He said AI is lowering the cost of attacks and making them faster and easier to scale. Donjon has begun using AI to find vulnerabilities, he added, noting that attackers are doing so as well.

data.title: Samuel Kerr Says Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Could Reverse AI Investment Pessimism
data.description: Mergermarket global equity capital markets head Samuel Kerr said Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO could reverse pessimism about AI investment. According to Odaily, AI-related stocks have sold off sharply since early October amid investor concerns that the industry’s rapid expansion could slow. Kerr said the listing may improve expectations for AI growth and related stocks, helping the bull market continue. He also said stronger overall market conditions would encourage other technology companies to pursue IPOs.

data.title: SoFi Survey: 21% of U.S. Gen Z Own Crypto, Exceeding Retirement Plan Ownership
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Decrypt, a SoFi survey released November 19 found that 21% of U.S. Gen Z adults own cryptocurrency, compared with 16% who have employer retirement plans such as 401(k)s. The Gen Z ownership rate was seven times the 3% reported among baby boomers, and crypto was the group’s most commonly held investment, ahead of stocks, bonds and real estate. SoFi and YouGov conducted the online survey from October 15 to 28 among 2,064 U.S. adults; SoFi and Culture Co-op jointly produced the report.

Among Gen Z respondents, 21% said crypto was one of the best ways to build future wealth, versus 8% of all respondents, and 61% viewed it as a financial advantage unique to their generation. Diversification motivated 32% of Gen Z crypto buyers, cross-border payment convenience 29%, and interest in trying something fun 20%. Overall, 13% of U.S. adults owned crypto, while 62% were firm skeptics and 77% said crypto felt like a financial side task they lacked time or energy to pursue. Half of crypto-open respondents said access through their primary bank could be a turning point, and 63% of current investors said they would trade more through a bank. SoFi has launched tokenized deposits yielding 4.4% and a bank-issued stablecoin operating on Polygon’s payments infrastructure. Ownership was 22% among Black and Hispanic respondents and 9% among White respondents; Miami led the 10 surveyed cities at 20%.

data.title: Anthropic Co-Founders' Combined Wealth Tops $140 Billion at $83 IPO Price
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bloomberg, Anthropic's seven co-founders have a combined net worth of more than $140 billion, or about $20 billion each, based on the company's IPO offering price of $83 per share. The Bloomberg Billionaires Index estimates that each founder holds an approximately 1.3% economic interest on a fully diluted basis.

The seven each sold about 3.38 million shares in the IPO, worth roughly $280 million apiece at the offering price. CEO Dario Amodei and Chair Daniela Amodei also participated in share tender offers in June 2025 and April 2026. Their remaining shares are subject to lockups of up to about one year for the founders and six months for current and former employees.

Although each founder holds about 1.3% of the economic interest, they retain 50.1% of the voting power on general matters submitted to shareholders through one Class F common share held by Founder LLC. The prospectus says the 2% ownership threshold for Founder LLC membership is calculated using each founder's and affiliated holders' Class A shares at the IPO's completion; founders below the threshold lose membership. Each founder has also pledged to devote 80% of their Anthropic equity to charity, but the pledges are voluntary, revocable, and not legally binding.

Less than two years ago, after Anthropic raised $3.5 billion at a $61.5 billion valuation, the seven founders became billionaires for the first time. After another financing round in May this year, all seven ranked among the Bloomberg Global Billionaires Index's top 500.

data.title: Hashi Bitcoin Finance Protocol Launches on Sui Mainnet
data.description: Hashi, a Bitcoin finance protocol on Sui, has launched on the Sui mainnet. According to Foresight News, Sui says users can deposit native BTC and receive hBTC on Sui for lending, collateral and other DeFi applications, while the underlying Bitcoin remains on the Bitcoin network. To withdraw, users burn hBTC and receive their native BTC. Mysten Labs developed the underlying infrastructure, while third parties independently build and provide related financial products.

data.title: STOCKS | Nvidia Says TSMC Executives Visited This Week
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Nvidia interim CEO Kress said TSMC executives visited the company’s offices this week and offered full cooperation and support. Kress also said the company raised its revenue growth guidance for the next fiscal year to 75%, from 70%. Analysts expect growth to slow to 33% the following year and 18% in the third year.

Kress said Nvidia’s Rubin chips generated $20 billion in revenue in their first quarter of volume production deliveries. Nvidia said cloud-provider orders on its books totaled $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months earlier. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri estimated that major global computing-infrastructure operators would spend about $1.76 trillion on capital expenditures next year, with a large portion expected to go to Nvidia.

Nvidia reported quarterly revenue and profit above Wall Street estimates, and its revenue guidance for the current quarter exceeded analysts’ forecasts. Kress said returning cash to shareholders was the company’s top priority, followed by supporting core suppliers that need prepayments or other financing. She said Nvidia would continue offering credit support and guarantees to customers, while carefully assessing participation and controlling capital commitments.

data.title: S&P Global Market Intelligence: Brent Forecast to Fall to $83 by End-2027
data.description: According to Jin10, S&P Global Market Intelligence expects Brent crude prices to fall to $83 per barrel by the end of 2027 and $70 by the end of 2028 as supply disruptions ease. Its November economic outlook incorporates a forecast from S&P Global Energy that spot Brent will be $110 per barrel in December 2026. The company said recent oil price declines could ease inflationary pressure, but major central banks are expected to continue raising interest rates. The Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan are expected to tighten policy further in December.
